axes.model_access:
**Model-agnosticism is its selling point: officially hosted models, BYOK, and local models coexist.**

Officially hosted models cover four vendors, plus an open-weight pool.

- Anthropic: Claude Opus / Sonnet / Fable / Haiku
- OpenAI: GPT-6 / GPT-5.5 / GPT-5.3-Codex
- Google: Gemini
- xAI: Grok
- Droid Core open weights: GLM, Kimi, Qwen, DeepSeek, MiniMax, Nemotron, etc.

Every model is labeled with its burn multiplier and supported `reasoningEffort`.

Multiplier examples: `gpt-5.5` is 2×, `claude-sonnet-5` is 0.8×.

**BYOK can use your own keys or any OpenAI-compatible endpoint.**

**Official wording**: "Use your own OpenAI or Anthropic keys, connect to any open source model providers, or run models locally"

Config lives in `customModels` in `~/.factory/settings.json`, three fields.

- `baseUrl`
- `apiKey`
- `provider` (one of three: `anthropic`, `openai`, `generic-chat-completion-api`)

Values can reference environment variables via `${VAR}`.

Any OpenAI-compatible endpoint works: OpenRouter / Fireworks / Together / Ollama / vLLM etc.

**API keys stay local and are not uploaded.**

**Official wording**: "Your API keys remain local and are not uploaded to Factory servers"

Switch models with `/model`.

**Custom models are CLI-only and do not appear on Web / mobile.**

There is also the official **Factory Router** for automatic cross-provider routing.
axes.runtime:
**CLI-first, but the official positioning is "one agent, multiple platforms".**

The workhorse is the terminal process `droid`, an interactive REPL.

Its lifecycle is bound to the terminal session — close the terminal and it ends.

Three install options:

- macOS / Linux: official script `curl -fsSL https://app.factory.ai/cli | sh`
- Windows: `irm https://app.factory.ai/cli/windows | iex`
- or npm: `npm install -g droid`

**The same agent has two more entry points.**

- **Factory App** — a desktop client
- **Droid SDK** — TypeScript `@factory/droid-sdk`, Python `droid-sdk`

The official pricing page lists all three as Pro-tier contents.

**Official wording**: "Factory App / Droid CLI / Droid SDK"

On the enterprise side there are also **Droid Computers**, Factory-managed remote cloud environments, from the Plus tier up.

**This entry documents the CLI form only**; desktop and SDK differences follow the official pages.
axes.local_files:
**It reads and writes in your own working directory; the official docs add two isolation mechanisms.**

One is `--cwd <path>`, setting the working directory.

Two is `-w, --worktree [name]`, running on a separate git worktree.

**Official wording**: "fanning out parallel `droid exec` jobs against the same repo without file conflicts"

Official note: clean worktrees are auto-deleted on exit; dirty ones are kept for review.

**Non-interactive `droid exec` is read-only by default.**

Read commands listed under the DEFAULT tier include:

- `cat` / `ls` / `git status` / `git log`
- `find`, but not with `-delete` / `-exec`

The official docs state plainly under the DEFAULT tier:

**Official wording**: "No modifications to files or system"

To change files you must explicitly raise it to `--auto low` or above.

**Whether the codebase is vector-indexed, and how long first indexing takes on large repos, is not stated officially**
(CLI Reference and Quickstart pages checked).
axes.background:
**The CLI itself is session-bound, but there is an explicit cloud background form officially.**

The terminal process ends on exit.

The official pricing page's Pro tier lists:

**Official wording**: "Cloud & local background agents"

The Plus tier unlocks **Droid Computers**.

**Official wording**: "Factory-managed Droid Computers (remote cloud environments)"

The enterprise page also says Droid can run on:

- CI runners, VMs, Kubernetes clusters

**Missions** is the multi-agent orchestration form: an orchestrator coordinates workers and validators.

Launch either via `/missions` or `droid exec --mission`.

The official docs require the High autonomy level, or `--skip-permissions-unsafe`.

**Concrete cloud concurrency numbers and quotas are not given by the official docs**
(Plans & Pricing and the Missions overview checked).
axes.tools:
**The built-in tool surface is broad, MCP support is complete, and there is an interactive manager.**

Built-in capabilities include:

- command execution, file read/write, git operations
- code review (`/review`)
- image generation, PDF reading

The extension surface adds five more classes:

- **Skills** — `/skills`, `/create-skill`
- **Hooks** — nine event types including PreToolUse / PostToolUse / PreCompact
- **Custom Droids sub-agents** — `/droids`
- **Plugins** — `/plugins`, distributed via a marketplace
- custom slash commands and **AGENTS.md**

**MCP supports two transports.**

**Official wording**: "Droid supports two types of servers: http (remote endpoints) and stdio (local processes)"

Add via `droid mcp add <name> <url> --type http` or `droid mcp add <name> "<command>"`.

`/mcp` opens the interactive manager: browse, inspect tools, enable/disable, do OAuth auth.

It can also add 40+ servers from a registry.

Config is two-layer: user-level `~/.factory/mcp.json` and project-level `.factory/mcp.json`.

There is also `disabledTools` to disable per tool; OAuth tokens are stored in the system keyring.

**Non-interactive mode is also officially supported.**

`droid exec` output formats are `text` / `json`.

There is also `--input-format stream-jsonrpc`, a long-lived JSON-RPC control plane.
axes.context:
**Sessions can be resumed by id and forked; compaction and the control plane are documented.**

On the non-interactive side, resume with `droid exec --session-id <id>`.

Fork with `--fork <id>`.

On the interactive side, exit prompts resume, and the CLI reference has `-r, --resume`.

The stream-jsonrpc control plane exposes `droid.load_session`, session forking and history compaction.

**Official wording**: "interrupt work, update settings, manage MCP servers/tools, inspect context, fork sessions, or compact history"

Compaction additionally has a `PreCompact` hook event.

The changelog also has this line:

**Official wording**: "in-place compression"

**On memory**, the official enterprise form mentions cross-repo "organizational knowledge".

There is also issue-tracker context.

The Enterprise tier additionally has:

**Official wording**: "Cross-harness agent memory"

**The persistence boundary and retention policy of memory on the CLI side are not stated on the CLI pages**
(CLI Overview and Droid Exec pages checked).
axes.permissions:
**Permissions are a two-level design: tiered autonomy (Autonomy Level) plus command allow/deny/block lists.**

Enterprises can additionally cap both levels.

The official Autonomy page splits execution risk into four tiers.

- **Off** — read-only tools + allowlisted commands
- **Low** — file edits + low-risk commands / MCP
- **Medium** — plus reversible workspace changes, e.g. `npm install`, `git commit`
- **High** — high-risk operations, e.g. `git push`, migrations

Switch by cycling with `Ctrl+L`; `Shift+Tab` toggles Auto / Spec.

Command policy is three tables.

- `commandAllowlist` — treated as low risk
- `commandDenylist` — requires approval even when relaxed
- `commandBlocklist` — **refused at any level, with no approval prompt**; sees through `bash -c` wrapper evasion

The official docs call `commandBlocklist`:

**Official wording**: "the strongest control available"

Non-interactive `droid exec` is read-only by default.

Open it up stepwise with `--auto low|medium|high`.

`--skip-permissions-unsafe` opens everything; officially labeled DANGEROUS, isolated environments only.

Exceeding the level stops immediately: non-zero exit code, no partial changes (fail-fast).

Enterprises can cap with Default / Maximum Autonomy Level.
axes.fit:
**Fits teams running end-to-end software engineering in the terminal and needing enterprise-grade governance.**

Three kinds of teams match best:

- those with existing repos who want the full plan → implement → test flow (`/missions` multi-agent orchestration)
- those automating CI/CD: `droid exec` one-shot runs, JSON output, non-zero exit on failure
- those needing BYOK / local models / airgapped deployment, to break free of single-vendor lock-in

**Not a fit** for individuals just wanting a free lightweight terminal assistant — there is no free tier officially; the lowest is the paid Pro tier.

**When citing a version number, state which surface.**

sections.安装与三种入口:
All three installs work:

```
curl -fsSL https://app.factory.ai/cli | sh      # macOS / Linux
irm https://app.factory.ai/cli/windows | iex    # Windows
npm install -g droid
```

**It is not "a CLI tool" but "one agent with three entry points".**

- the pricing page writes Pro-tier contents as "Factory App / Droid CLI / Droid SDK"
- the official docs also have "IDE Integrations" with JetBrains / Zed integrations

When purchasing, check which entry point you want: the three do not have identical execution surfaces or quota accounting.
sections.额度不是「每月一个总量」:
The official quota is a **three-window rolling Rate Limit**:

```
5-hour / 7-day / 30-day windows are independent; all must have headroom for a request to go through
```

**This explains "why I'm still rate-limited right after topping up"** — you may be hitting the 5-hour window.

When rate-limited you can switch to **Droid Core** and keep working: it is an open-weight model pool with its own free quota.

You can also use **Extra Usage**: prepaid, never expires (minimum top-up on the official page; per this site's D9 rule, not stored here).

This is one of the finest-grained quota schemes this site has seen.
sections.企业形态:
The official Enterprise page writes the deployment surface as:

> "cloud, hybrid, and fully airgapped environments"

Droid can run on:

> "developer laptops, CI runners, VMs, Kubernetes clusters, airgapped networks"

The compliance-program table lists **SOC 2 Type II / ISO 27001 / ISO 42001**.

The official docs also offer Droid Shield, command policies, hooks, sandboxing and OpenTelemetry telemetry.

**This is the most complete enterprise-governance narrative in this section**, though all of it is vendor self-description.
